description: The Athens Trees Information System is a web map of the Municipality of Athens that records the trees the city plants, so residents can see where new street and park trees go. The page read on 2026-09-28 counts 13,233 trees planted since 1 January 2024 against a yearly target of 10,000, lets users filter plantings on the map by municipal community and tree type, and lists the latest plantings with date, address, community and species (for example photinia and bougainvillea planted on 16 September 2026); clicking a planting shows its details. Coverage is the seven municipal communities of the City of Athens, point by point, and updated continuously. Access is a free web viewer on an OpenStreetMap base; the page offers no download or API and names no licence, so reuse terms are unclear. Caveats: it covers new plantings, not the full existing tree stock, and attributes such as size or condition are not shown. It supports climate adaptation studies of urban heat and green infrastructure, for example tracking canopy growth along streets and near public buildings. Related records: street tree inventories of other cities such as data-copenhagen-street-trees and data-buenos-aires-trees-in-green-spaces offer comparable data with downloads.
